outcome: Store traffic reaches cloud services directly instead of via head office, with paths chosen automatically as circuit quality changes.
overview: Retail branch networking was designed when applications lived in a data centre, and it still routes as though they do — traffic for a cloud point-of-sale service travels to head office and back out. Prisma SD-WAN selects a path per application from measurements taken continuously rather than failing over only on a link drop, and its policy is expressed in terms of applications rather than routes. For a chain, the practical test is whether a store manager notices anything: the design succeeds when nobody calls about the till being slow.

benefits.text: Cloud-hosted retail applications reach their service directly rather than via head office
benefits.limits: Local breakout changes the security path as well as the network path, and the two decisions have to be made together

benefits.text: Path selection responds to measured degradation, not only to a link failing outright
benefits.limits: Requires genuinely diverse circuits; two services on the same physical path degrade together and no overlay can compensate

benefits.text: Policy is authored per application, so a change reaches every store consistently
benefits.limits: Central policy is also a central blast radius; ring-based rollout of policy changes is part of the design rather than an option

residency: Overlay controller is vendor-operated while traffic stays on customer circuits; the controller region is a recorded design decision

notFor.situation: A chain already running an SD-WAN overlay
notFor.why: Overlays do not interwork, so a change means running two networks through a long transition

notFor.situation: Stores with a single circuit and no plan for a second
notFor.why: Path selection needs paths; with one circuit the overlay adds management without the benefit

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Palo Alto Networks implementation partner · Duration: 10–14 weeks to a proven pilot ring; rollout at an agreed stores-per-week rate
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with a replacement term suited to store criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed overlay operations.
1) Assessment — circuit inventory and diversity verification, application classification, store throughput measurement
2) Design — overlay topology, per-application policy, breakout and security pairing, ring model
3) Pilot — first ring on the overlay with rollback proven
4) Roll out and hand over — chain rollout by ring, controller policy under change control, operations handed over
